routes.native: solver.saveat=21600 s with native saveat-aligned UserDemand application
routes.explicit_apply: solver.saveat=86400 s with 21600 s BMI boundaries and test-only explicit UserDemand/per-link apply

equivalence: For each priority case, native and explicit-apply routes produced identical logged Basin level, storage gain and cumulative recipient-delivery values at 6, 12, 18 and 24 h.
qualified_claims: The test-only explicit UserDemand solve→apply seam is segment-by-segment transactionally equivalent to native 6-hour saveat application for the tested one-day cases.
Final endpoint agreement is not compensating error; the accepted physical state and cumulative transfer ledger match at every 6-hour boundary.
Output record cadence and UserDemand application cadence are separable in the demonstrated contract.
The necessary coupling primitive is an explicit allocation application/commit at the accepted management boundary, not an allocation output write.
architectural_contract: SOLVE: compute a candidate allocation from the accepted current physical state.
APPLY/ADMIT: explicitly publish the selected UserDemand allocation and per-link targets to the physical model state.
REALIZE: advance physical dynamics using that applied allocation.
ACCEPT/COMMIT: accept the resulting physical state and transfer ledger at the coupling boundary.
RECORD: emit diagnostics/output independently of the semantic commit, unless a product API intentionally couples them.
boundaries: This proves equivalence for the tested UserDemand topology and pinned Ribasim only.
The explicit helper is research code, not a production Ribasim API.
downstream: Update the programme synthesis and use solve→apply→realize→accept→record as the research contract for the next real-coupler substitution work.
